item.title: ‘Take the blame’ – Former NBA champion calls Doc Rivers ‘weird’ for Giannis Antetokounmpo comments
item.description: Photo by Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images Doc Rivers’ seemingly critical comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo have created massive discourse, and one former Laker has taken exception to what he said. It is very rare that people within the NBA fraternity speak negatively about one another to the media. Whatever the issues are behind the scenes, they tend not to come out. So when Doc Rivers was recently critical of his former superstar, Giannis Antetokounmpo, the situation blew up quickly. Rivers made comments about the difficulty of coaching the Greek Freak and seemingly called out his playing style. Antetokounmpo was visibly shocked when told of the comments, calling them ‘insane’. Doc has since reportedly apologised, but fans and the media alike have a lot to say about the issue. Metta Sandiford-Artest asks coaches to stop blaming players after Doc Rivers’ comments The relationship between players and coaches in the NBA can be tenuous at times. It is rarely worse than when a team with expectations fails to deliver, like the Milwaukee Bucks did during Rivers’ tenure. There is plenty of blame to go around in those situations, and nobody really wants it. Regardless, for Rivers to suggest openly that Giannis is difficult to coach is something a lot of people have taken issue with. And former NBA champion Metta Sandiford-Artest has vocalised the issue. “Weird that a person would throw Giannis Antetokounmpo under the bus,” Sandiford-Artest wrote in a post on X. “Makes no sense. All he does is work hard and (bring) championships to the Milwaukee. Coach Metta so ready to take the blame. Coaches, stop blaming players.” The former Laker currently works as a coach in women’s college basketball, which may explain why he is weighing in on the matter. Rivers himself has clarified his comments since he made them, but that doesn’t mean that everyone in the basketball world will let them slide. Read more: ‘Life is short’ – Stephen A. item.title: The strange reason Japan can’t pick their best fly half against England
item.description: In the aftermath of his side’s defeat to Wales, the Japan head coach Eddie Jones already had more than half an eye on England . “We’ll need to be able to break up the game,” the veteran schemer said with a glint in his eye and a familiar smirk on his face. “If we play an orthodox game of rugby, we’re probably going to struggle to beat them. And the English don’t react well to unorthodox rugby. We’ve got to think about how we can play quite unorthodoxly.” Jones speaks, of course, from experience. It was his England side that were baffled by Italy’s radical ruck tactics in the Six Nations in 2017 ; in a neat twist, Conor O’Shea, the architect of that plan, now heads up performance at England’s Rugby Football Union (RFU). “Maybe we’ll play like Italy did in 2017,” Jones teased. “Can you still play like that in the rucks? I don’t think you can, can you?” Eddie Jones has promised to throw a few curveballs at England (Getty) England are bracing for something similarly avant-garde nonetheless. It is instructive, though, that Jones is having to talk in such terms about a side he does not yet see as an equal to the world’s top teams. Japan beat Italy and pushed Ireland close in July, before coming within three points of Australia in August – they have the talent to at least give England a fright. There is one key difference from those games, though. In each of those encounters, Japan were steered from fly half by Ryunosuke Ito, a 21-year-old playmaker long tipped for a bright future who was named to start against France before he had even played a senior club game. He took to Test rugby like a natural; through the Nations Championship, Australia series and Pacific Nations Cup, the No 10 shirt was his. For a team that had struggled to replace Yu Tamura, and with Lee Seung Sin injured, here was the welcome emergence of a new, young star. Ryunosuke Ito has emerged as a budding star for Japan (Getty) That flourishing has been brought to a strange and unwelcome halt, though. Ito is not in the United Kingdom with the rest of Jones’s squad, with Riku Kitahara steering the ship against Wales in Cardiff instead. Kitahara performed well; about as well as one might expect of a player reportedly described by Jones as his fourth-choice fly half. There is no injury to speak of to Ito. Why, then, is he absent? Well, it has to do with a strange rugby hierarchy that persists in Japan. While his colleagues are battling the best in men’s Test rugby in Europe, Ito will be obliged to pull on the shirt of Meiji University as he completes his education. “He’s the only 10 for a tier one nation in the world who has to go and play for an amateur team now,” Jones complained after the recent defeat to Fiji, according to rugbyjp.com . “Imagine if [baseball superstar] Shohei Ohtani went back to play for Keio University.” It is a challenge that just about every homegrown Japan international faces. item.title: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez is quietly having a Pro Bowl year
item.description: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team , the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams . And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati Bengals, twice. RELATED: BOJORQUEZ INTERVIEW Consider the fact that there aren’t any really good teams left on their schedule. Could they still make the playoffs? A division title seems out of reach, but it takes 10 or 11 wins to get that #7 seed, and they are already halfway to that goal. There are several players on the Browns roster who are having a good year. Guys like TE Harold Fannin, LBs Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, plus DT Mason Graham are getting their fair share of press regarding possibly getting some major Pro Bowl votes. But one player stands out, and nobody is talking about his season: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. The Boot is back 🥾 We've re-signed P Corey Bojorquez! 📰 Read more: https://t.co/wQ4NPLBAHA pic.twitter.com/r7RsK8WdCa — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) March 12, 2026 Guys who make their living on special teams are usually only noticed when they miss a field goal, or both a punt, or skip a pass to the holder. Bojo has quietly been killing it as Cleveland’s punter this season. He was re-signed during last March’s free agency period. Currently, he is listed #5 in the league in net average per punt with 44.0 yards. The league leader is just 46.1, so Bojorquez is keeping the rankings tight. He is ranked #4 in average distance per kick at 50.4. Again, the leader’s number is close at 51.8, so one game could alter these numbers. Usually, the punters with the most kicks in a season are on teams whose offensive units can’t finish drives, or are unable to sustain drives. Bojo is ranked #3 in the most punts with 43. The league leader plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, which backs up this stat goes to guys who are on struggling offensive teams. He booted a season-high eight punts in the loss to the New York Jets when the offense could not move the ball. Bojo is considered a field flipper . This means his kicks can alter the opposing team’s field position just off one punt that has traveled 50+ yards. Case in point, in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, Bojorquez’s first punt was for 68 yards. Pretty good, eh? His first punt of the second half was 60 yards. Then his final kick was for a whopping 81 yards that went from Cleveland’s 19-yard line into the end zone. item.title: Hollywood Legend LeVar Burton Has Five Special Words For WNBA Champion Gabby Williams
item.description: Nov 4, 2026; San Francisco, California, US; Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams holds the WNBA most valuable player trophy during the Golden State Valkyries championship parade. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Gabby Williams has not had a quiet week. Since the Golden State Valkyries won the WNBA championship, tributes have rolled in from sports, entertainment, and politics. Michael Jordan sent a text, Stephen Curry cheered the team on, and Barack Obama posted his praise online. Now, a Reading Rainbow legend has joined the list. LeVar Burton congratulated the Finals MVP in a short video that CBS Mornings shared on X. Both were guests on the broadcast. Burton was there to discuss his memoir, Take My Word For It, while Williams was celebrating the Valkyries’ historic run. Burton kept it brief, but the warmth came through. He shook Williams’ hand and delivered his message. “ Congratulations. Really. And I’ve got to say, you are carrying this like a queen. You really are ,” Burton said. “ Congratulations. Many more years of success, or as many as you would like to have. ” SPECIAL MOMENT: Legendary actor and “Reading Rainbow” host @levarburton congratulated Golden State @valkyries star Gabby Williams on her WNBA championship win. Williams was named the 2026 @WNBA Finals MVP after helping lead the Valkyries to their first championship in franchise history. — CBS Mornings (@CBSMornings) November 9, 2026 Burton then introduced his wife, Stephanie, who congratulated Williams as well. Williams answered with a simple thank-you. “ We’re going to come see you next season ,” Burton said. Burton has plenty to cheer. Golden State beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 on Oct. 31 at Chase Center. The Valkyries won the title in their second season, a feat described as the fastest by an expansion franchise in major American pro sports. Williams made it happen the hard way. She had 2 points at halftime, and Golden State trailed 30-24. She then scored 28 in the second half, a WNBA postseason record for a single half. She finished with 30. Williams said the break did not rattle her. Coach Natalie Nakase delivered a fiery message, but Williams saw a six-point gap and believed that if she got going, her team would be fine. She was right. Atlanta tied it in the fourth quarter, and Williams answered with a deep three with 2:18 left to make it 60-57. The Valkyries never trailed again. What The Title Means For Gabby Williams After 8 Seasons Of Waiting This was Williams’ eighth WNBA season and her first in Golden State, following three in Chicago and four in Seattle. The wait stretched beyond the league, too. France lost the 2024 Olympic gold medal game to the United States by one point, then lost to the Americans again in the FIBA Women’s World Cup final in September. Williams also won the EuroLeague title with Fenerbahçe in April. Even so, the WNBA trophy was the one she wanted most. The Finals MVP averaged 19.6 points and 2.6 steals in the series.

item.title: Valentino Rossi in new autobiography: '2015 still hurts, Marc Marquez wanted me to lose'
item.description: Motorsport photo Valentino Rossi has revisited his 2015 feud with Marc Marquez in his new autobiography, maintaining that the Spaniard interfered in his MotoGP title battle with Jorge Lorenzo . The nine-time world champion previously published a book about his career while he was still at the peak of his powers. But a new work, La Mia Storia , will be released on 10 November, offering a fresh account of the defining moments of a legendary and often controversial career. Although 11 years have passed, the events of the 2015 Malaysian Grand Prix remain a defining chapter in the Italian's life. Rossi was fighting Lorenzo for what would have been his 10th world title and arrived at Sepang accusing Marquez, with whom he had already been involved in several contentious incidents in Argentina and Assen that year, of conspiring to ensure a Spanish rider won the MotoGP championship. Marquez responded with an uncompromising battle during Sunday's race, which culminated in the infamous clash in which Rossi appeared to kick the Honda rider off his bike. Rossi believed Marquez, who was already out of title contention, was solely intent on losing him the championship. Rossi was subsequently penalised with a back-of-the-grid start in the Valencia finale, where tensions reached unprecedented levels between the three protagonists and among the fans who had travelled to the circuit. The race attracted record television audiences worldwide and ended with Lorenzo being crowned champion, while Rossi accused Marquez of a 'biscotto' – an alleged agreement to avoid attacking Lorenzo and prevent the title from going to the Italian. Rossi appeared on RAI's Che tempo che fa programme on Sunday to promote his new autobiography, which looks back on his sporting career. Inevitably, the interviewer asked him about the events of 2015. Rossi insisted that his version of events had not changed, admitting that what happened still hurts and that he regrets how much attention is devoted to the title he lost rather than the championships he won. item.title: Bryson DeChambeau Speaks As LIV Golf Files For Bankruptcy
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Bryson DeChambeau has confirmed his exit from LIV Golf as the league files for bankruptcy and scraps plans for a reboot. Lawyers representing the company told a New Jersey court on Thursday that the tour will wind down operations and enter liquidation. The move ends years of speculation about a second version of the breakaway circuit. DeChambeau posted a statement on X on Sunday, thanking fans and staff while refusing to change his past actions. To commit to the 2027 DP World Tour season, the American golfer must declare his intention by November 15. If he misses this deadline, he risks being frozen out of professional golf entirely. This timeline comes after the Saudi Public Investment Fund stopped its $5 billion support in April. BC Partners had pledged $300 million to back a new launch, but the firm pulled out when players did not sign on in time. A Statement on Four Years DeChambeau defended his choice to leave the PGA Tour and join LIV from the start. He thanked the staff, caddies, and operations crews who bet their careers on the new league. “I’m not going to rewrite the last four years,” DeChambeau wrote, according to Sky Sports . He noted that the record crowds in Adelaide and Johannesburg would stick with him for the rest of his life. He believes the game could reach more people in new ways, and he still holds that view. The former U.S. Open champion gave everything he had to keep team golf alive. He thanked his Crushers GC teammates and sponsors for their support. Despite the liquidation, he remained quiet about his own future plans. Arnold Palmer stated that no player is bigger than the game, according to his acknowledgment. DeChambeau admitted he said some things that did not help along the way and promised to move forward with humility. The Path Back to the Tour The PGA Tour will not reopen its Returning Member Program to let LIV players back in easily. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp stated earlier this year that the tour is a membership organization with strict rules. “The tour is a membership organization,” Rolapp said, according to AOL.com . He noted that rules only matter if they are enforced, and accountability is essential for the integrity of the game. A public decision on a return pathway is not expected until at least January. Adam Scott expressed a clear view on how former LIV golfers should return to the main circuit. item.title: The Lakers' continue to have one big problem despite their success
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers have a 10-2 record after downing the Atlanta Hawks 124-114 on Monday despite being without Austin Reaves, who sat out due to an illness. They now have the best record in the NBA, as well as the league's highest scoring average, offensive rating and overall field-goal accuracy. But there still seems to be the suspicion across the league that the Lakers aren't a championship-caliber team. While L.A. has defeated teams with good records such as the Hawks, Detroit Pistons , Golden State Warriors and Portland Trail Blazers , it still has issues that have to be sorted out before it gets to the next level. Los Angeles doesn't have a legitimate third scoring option alongside Reaves and Luka Doncic in the starting lineup. It also ranks 19th in defensive rating, although it is second in opponents' turnover percentage and first in points off turnovers per game. But the Lakers continue to have another weakness that has plagued them over the last few years, and it is one that will hurt them when they play against true contenders, as well as during the playoffs. L.A. is still weak on the boards Over the last few years, the Lakers have had problems in the rebounding department, and in the early going of this season, those problems have continued. Through Monday, they're 22nd in rebounding percentage and 28th in defensive rebounding percentage. While they have improved to 15th in offensive rebounding percentage, they continue to get outrebounded or merely play their opponents to a relative draw in the rebounding department on a regular basis. Los Angeles is 28th in the league in opponents' second-chance points per game. The team continues to be weak in all these areas even though new center Walker Kessler has been as good as advertised. He's averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 boards, 2.3 blocks and 1.3 steals in 30.9 minutes a game. A big reason for this lack of rebounding is the fact that the Lakers simply lack forwards who are strong on the boards, as well as a competent backup center. They have been using Sandro Mamukelashvili, who is 6-foot-10 and 240 pounds, as a backup center, and while he's a decent rebounder, he also isn't a force in that category. Other than Kessler and Doncic, none of the Lakers' regular rotation players average over seven rebounds per 36 minutes. Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Ziaire Williams, who have started games at forward this season, are underwhelming rebounders. Forward Jarred Vanderbilt is capable of getting rebounds in bunches, but due to his extreme limitations on offense, he doesn't receive and shouldn't receive more than spot-duty minutes. The only real way for the Lakers to rectify this lack of rebounding is to make a trade, but that will take a while. The NBA's trade market historically doesn't heat up until after Dec. 15, which is the earliest date that players signed as free agents during that year's offseason can be traded. Until then, L.A. will have to find other ways to win the possession battle

item.title: Watch: Alejandro Balde left surprised as Flick decided to bring De Jong at right-back against Atletico Madrid
item.description: Watch: Alejandro Balde left surprised as Flick decided to bring De Jong at right-back against Atletico Madrid Alejandro Balde’s reaction to Hansi Flick’s unexpected decision to deploy Frenkie de Jong at right-back against Atletico Madrid offered another glimpse into the Barcelona defender’s uncertain position under the German coach. As De Jong learned about his new role during the half-time team talk, Balde watched the conversation closely, appearing serious as the tactical change was explained. The moment was particularly notable because Balde is a natural left-back who has struggled to secure regular minutes this season. With Joao Cancelo capable of playing on either flank, Flick could have made a conventional defensive adjustment by moving the Portuguese defender to the right and introducing Balde on the left. Instead, he chose De Jong , leaving the Spaniard on the bench. Balde watches as Flick turns to De Jong Broadcast footage captured the reactions on the Barcelona bench when the coaching staff informed De Jong that he would be playing at right-back. The Dutchman initially appeared surprised but accepted the instruction, later explaining the change to teammates Gavi and Wojciech Szczesny. Balde was also listening attentively as the decision became clear. His reaction stood out because the situation could have presented a possible opportunity for him to enter the game, yet Flick opted for a midfielder who had previously filled the centre-back role. It would be speculative to claim exactly what Balde was thinking, but what can be safely assumed is that he would not be entirely happy. Balde’s Barcelona situation remains uncertain De Jong played as a right-back against Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The decision also needs to be viewed against Balde’s recent lack of involvement. Joao Cancelo has become Flick’s preferred option at left-back after Xavi Espart’s injury, while the Spaniard has struggled to establish himself in the starting XI. As a result, his situation has attracted attention in the transfer market, and on that note, we have reported earlier that Balde is open to a January departure if it offers him the opportunity to play regularly and rebuild his confidence, and he certainly does not lack suitors. Indeed, the decision to bring on De Jong at right-back worked well for Barcelona , but it clearly showed that Flick is not at all counting on Balde.

item.title: Khawaja alleges racial abuse by MCC member
item.description: Usman Khawaja played 88 Tests for Australia [Getty Images] Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja has alleged he was racially abused by a Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) member during the Ashes Test at Lord's in 2023. The incident came after England's Jonny Bairstow was controversially stumped by Australia wicketkeeper Alex Carey in the second Test, and Khawaja describes the members as like "a pack of dogs" in his newly released autobiography. Television footage at the time showed Khawaja and David Warner were involved in clashes with spectators as Australia walked off for lunch. As a result, the MCC expelled one member and suspended two others . They were all found to have used "abusive, offensive or inappropriate behaviour or language", with one member given a four-and-a-half-year suspension and the other serving 30 months. But Khawaja goes on to say he told one man not to shout at him again, which resulted in another person racially abusing him. "We didn't realise what was waiting for us in the Long Room. Unfortunately, the MCC members in the room that day showed their true colours," Khawaja said. "All of us always talked so highly of the MCC members, who were usually the kindest, most gentle, cricket-loving members in the world. You could get a hundred or a duck and they'd clap you as you walked off, all the same. It was a pleasure to be amongst them. "And it still is, but that day made us think maybe they aren't so different to the rest. Because when cricket, and the Lord's cricket ground, needed their civility the most, they turned into a pack of privileged drunks, barking at us from a metre away. "It was like a pack of dogs about to feast on their next meals. They were in unison, swearing. I couldn't believe what I was hearing." He then describes someone "shouting, spitting and screaming" in his face and that another member tried to trip him and Warner up as they walked up the stairs. "[He was] sticking his leg out, so we'd fall on the steps. Davey told him off first, so I didn't think the bloke would do it again. "But as I went to walk upstairs, he tried to do it to me too! "At the top of the stairs, I saw a whole bunch of members waiting for us near the change-room. I looked at them with a smile of shock, put my arms in the air, and said, 'Is this Lord's or the zoo?'" In his autobiography, Khawaja also claimed the entire Australia team knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball in the final Test of their 2018 series with South Africa. item.title: Cam Newton launching ‘4th & 1 Presents: Quarterback Club’ series on Amazon Prime
item.description: Credit: 4th&1 Former NFL MVP and Heisman Trophy winner Cam Newton, who’d become a regular feature on First Take , was one of the more surprising cuts in ESPN’s summer 2025 layoffs after signing a multi-year contract . Newton has taken the high road following his departure, insisting that nobody could make him hate t the network that gave him a chance, while remaining a presence in the media via his 4th & 1 podcast. On Monday, Deadline reported that Newton would be increasing that presence with 4th & 1 Presents: Quarterback Club, a weekly series in which he’ll speak with “past, present, and future” quarterbacks about one of the most high-pressure positions in all of sport. Quarterback Club will bring together rookies, established veterans, and “retired legends” every Tuesday at Iconic Saga Studios in Atlanta to “unpack the pressures, mental hurdles, and triumphs of playing the position against the backdrop of their own experiences and careers.” The first episode of the series will be available to stream on Prime Video on Wednesday, November 11th, with future episodes releasing every Wednesday; premiere dates, trailers, and additional guest details will be announced every Thursday. “Quarterbacks carry a city every Sunday, then get a few minutes at a podium to explain it,” Newton said. “ Quarterback Club is the room where we can finally be honest, with each other and with the fans.” Quarterback Club is produced in-house by Iconic Saga Productions, with Cam Newton, Derrick Brown, Travis Montaque, Rudy Vegliante, and RJ Mathis II serving as executive producers, per Deadline, with Creator Sports Entertainment Network (CSEN) assisting with distribution. “There are football shows, debate shows, and podcasts, but there has never been a room where quarterbacks can sit down peer-to-peer and candidly talk to each other about what it actually takes to play the game,” Derrick Brown said. item.description: Credit: Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Emilee Chinn via Getty Images ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith has addressed his pre-existing feud with Philadelphia 76ers’ LeBron James, burying the hatchet with the 41-year-old superstar. LeBron and Stephen A. had a very public dispute over the last two years, primarily because of Smith’s harsh takes on Bronny James, as well as years of tension through their player-journalist relationship. Despite the strong public comments and disagreements from both sides, it seems Smith is letting go of his negative feelings towards LeBron. Stephen A. Smith makes his feelings on LeBron James clear On the latest episode of ‘The Stephen A. Smith Show,’ the 59-year-old ESPN personality made it clear that he is no longer holding onto his issues with LeBron and wishes he leads the 76ers to an NBA title. “We all know that I’ve had my issues with LeBron James and vice versa. I do not hate the man. I was pissed off once upon a time, but I’m thoroughly over that. I’m 59 years old. Life is short. Ain’t got time for all of that. I wish him nothing but the best. And I’m looking forward to covering him as his career comes to an end over the next two years. Hopefully, he’ll win a championship for Philadelphia” Smith has strong ties to Philadelphia, starting his career as a writer for The Philadelphia Inquirer, where he actively covered the Allen Iverson-led 76ers for years before moving to national sports coverage with ESPN. Even if he held on to his personal differences, Smith will ultimately root for the 76ers to finally win an NBA Championship. Making amends with LeBron is the best way to enjoy that, as his addition has given Philly its best shot at a title in decades. Smith and LeBron’s feud started in 2025 over strong criticism of Bronny, which led to LeBron physically confronting Smith courtside at a Lakers vs. Knicks game in March 2025. James also posted mocking videos of Smith’s poor boxing form on social media. item.description: After the Falcons traded away Jessie Bates yesterday, Kevin Stefanski had to get in front of microphones and talk to reporters about two seemingly contrary thoughts: The team is not “punting” on the 2026 season, in his words, but they couldn’t pass up the chance to trade one of their most impactful defenders nine weeks into that season. Those two warring thoughts, captured well in Tori McElhaney’s piece for AtlantaFalcons.com , seem difficult to square when you first look at them. How could trading Jessie Bates not undercut Atlanta’s 2026 fortunes? A team looking to take full advantage of a weak NFC South should be trying to acquire talent, not sell, right? Right? But spending a little more time with the seeming divide between selling off and contending reveals a simple truth: Their division is a gallon jug of steamed butt. If we’re being real about what’s happening here, the Falcons aren’t quitting on 2026 because it’s impossible to quit on 2026 in the NFC South. They are one game behind the Carolina Panthers, thanks to a head-to-head tiebreaker, and just a half game behind the New Orleans Saints. It’s not completely outlandish to suggest seven wins could actually earn the divisional title this year, and the Falcons are certainly good enough in their best weeks to win four out of their next eight games with matchups against the Browns, Commanders, diminished Lions, and rest of the NFC South still on the docket. If they continue to sell, as Carl Dukes at 92.9 suggested they would , it does nothing to change the fact that they’re still a team with some promising pieces and the same number of wins as everyone else in the division, and they have young players they wouldn’t mind getting a look at dotting the roster. That’s certainly true at safety, where Sydney Brown, Billy Bowman Jr., and DeMarcco Hellams could all be in the mix for snaps. It could prove true at inside linebacker, where the Falcons have been getting plenty from Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. and may be willing to move Divine Deablo. It might be true at tackle, where the Falcons could potentially move Jawaan Taylor or even Jake Matthews if they get a really interesting offer and turn to Mike Jerrell, Cameron Williams, or Ethan Onianwa, though the prospect of Michael Penix Jr. getting pressured even more frequently is not an appealing one.
